newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU presses U.S. to implement meat trade deal.
newsitem.headline: EU presses U.S. to implement meat trade deal.

text.p: The European Union on Tuesday pressed the United States to fully implement an agreement on mutually acceptable meat inspection rules, EU officials said.
They added that the EU would also soon complain to the World Trade Organisation about U.S. curbs on some $1 million worth of imports of EU poultry products, mainly French chicken pate and foie gras.

At a meeting of EU farm ministers, France, supported by Germany, Austria, Spain, Italy, Greece and Luxembourg, criticised the meat inspection deal struck by the European Commission on April 3 as unbalanced.
France complained that Washington had not said when it would recognise EU regional, rather than national, trade curbs following outbreaks of animal and plant diseases
The EU has agreed to immediately implement the so-called veterinary equivalency agreement after it has been signed. Signature is foreseen in the autumn.

EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler will write to his U.S. counterpart, Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman, warning that the EU may rescind the agreement if Washington has not adopted the regionalisation principle within 12 months of signature, a Commission spokesman said.
